dependentSpeciesLedger.title: The tenant ledger of one fallen tree
dependentSpeciesLedger.subtitle: Fix the doomed total on the day of the felling, then walk a census forward and watch it discover them
dependentSpeciesLedger.hint: Koh and colleagues found the shape of a dependent species' response turns on how fussy it is: a strict obligate goes one-for-one with its host, while a species that can use several hosts hangs on until the whole host network collapses. Tilman named the delay extinction debt — the destruction happens now, the extinctions are paid later, by instalment. Scrub the years and the two numbers separate: what a clipboard would record, and what was already owed.

infectionBarrierGauntlet.title: The infection chain, lock by lock
infectionBarrierGauntlet.subtitle: Try each lock in turn and find out where the chain actually ends
infectionBarrierGauntlet.pairingLabel: Which pair of organisms is meeting

exposure.name: Reach the right tissue
exposure.detail: Breath, a mouthful, a bite or a cut has to put the organism somewhere it can act. Landing on intact skin is not exposure.

docking.name: Recognise a surface it can hold
docking.detail: Adhesins, pili and viral coat proteins have to fit particular molecules on the host's cells. This is a lock cut by shared evolutionary history, and nothing else cuts it.

chemistry.name: Survive the host's chemistry
chemistry.detail: Temperature, acidity, salt, digestive enzymes. A microbe built for cool wet soil is not built for the inside of a warm animal.

replication.name: Copy itself using what is there
replication.detail: A virus borrows the host's ribosomes and enzymes outright. A bacterium at least needs molecules it can recognise as food. Mismatched machinery stops replication dead.

immunity.name: Get past the broad defences
immunity.detail: Engulfing cells, reactive chemistry and membrane-tearing peptides attack anything unfamiliar. These need no prior acquaintance with the invader, which is exactly why they catch strangers.

transmission.name: Leave in a viable form
transmission.detail: One infected body is a dead end unless offspring get out and reach somebody else. Without this the outbreak has a population of one.

blocked.exposure: It never reached tissue where it could do anything. The chain ends before it starts.
blocked.docking: Nothing on the host's cells fits it. Without a shared evolutionary history there is no handle to grip, and every lock behind this one is unreachable.
blocked.chemistry: The host's internal chemistry destroys it before it can do anything else.
blocked.replication: It cannot use this host's molecular machinery, so it cannot make copies. A pathogen that cannot replicate is a particle, not an infection.
blocked.immunity: The host's broad, unspecific defences clear it. They never needed to have met it before.
blocked.transmission: It infected one body and had no way out. That is a dead end, not an epidemic.

verdict.start: Nothing has happened yet. Open the first lock and see how far a visitor gets.
verdict.walking: {n, plural, =1 {One lock open. It had to open before any of the others could be tried.} other {# locks open so far, and every one of them had to open in order.}}

outcome.sameBiosphere: All six open — which is how a host jump happens on Earth. Note that two of them were narrow: shared ancestry makes this possible, not easy, and most microbes still cannot infect most species.
outcome.crossBiosphere: Never reached. Two biospheres with separate origins share no receptors, no molecular handedness and no genetic code, so the chain ends at the first recognition step.
outcome.avatarChimera: Never reached, and not because the answer is no. Nobody has measured it.

infectionBarrierGauntlet.harmLead: None of these need the organism to reproduce inside a living host, so failing every lock above rules none of them out. "Cannot infect" and "cannot harm" are different claims.

harm.necrotrophy: Digesting dead tissue at a wound
harm.fouling: Fouling a membrane until it cannot work
harm.niche: Taking an ecological niche nothing here defends
